match.header: What can I do with Poppy — and why is it useful?

set.header: What can I do with Poppy — and why is it useful?
set.bodytext:
Think of Poppy as an agent’s identity check and a limited permission slip. A website can recognise which personal agent is visiting and which person it represents. The person chooses the access to grant; the business chooses the actions it offers.

  • Ask before signing in: read product facts, opening hours or published support guidance through a guest session.
  • Continue with permission: a future account integration could offer returns, appointments or order changes, limited to the access the person approved.
  • Keep one visit across channels: the protocol is designed to carry the session between a website, APIs and a business’s own agent.

Try it here: our current TYPO3 profile reads two published explanations. It starts and renews a verified guest session and rejects reused request proofs. It does not book appointments, change accounts or edit TYPO3. The playground is a real protocol test; it does not need a language model.

Poppy gives personal agents a shared way to discover a website, identify themselves and work within the access the website offers. TYPO3 Lab implements the signed-out profile of draft 0.1: verified guest sessions and a read-only OpenAPI endpoint for published explanations.

Our first use case is simple: ask what the lab says about Poppy or Pi Durable and receive the CMS text with its source URL. A separate TYPO3 extension handles the protocol. Editors own the explanation in normal TYPO3 content records.

This release offers public knowledge, with no account sign-in or editing permissions. Browser visitors remain ordinary signed-out visitors. Poppy is an early draft, so we document the supported profile and test its security boundaries.

set.header: From discovery to a sourced answer
set.content: The agent reads the discovery document and checks the issuer. It proves its identity, starts a guest session and signs its API request. TYPO3 returns the published explanation with a link back to this page.

media.title: From discovery to a sourced answer
media.description: Four steps: discover poppy.json; verify identity and start a guest session; send a DPoP proof; read published TYPO3 content and its source.

set.bodytext:
1. Discover: the personal agent reads /.well-known/poppy.json and learns the issuer and available API.
  2. Identify: TYPO3 verifies the registered agent’s signature and its separate user-session assertion.
  3. Start a guest session: the agent gets a short-lived token tied to its own DPoP key. A copied token alone is insufficient.
  4. Ask the lab: a signed request selects Poppy or Pi Durable. TYPO3 reads the published “What TYPO3 Lab says” section and returns the text and source.
  5. Continue safely: the agent renews its session when necessary. Reusing a request proof is rejected.

Run these steps in the playground. Use “See the requests” to inspect the actual responses.

Open the live Poppy playground. Ask about Poppy or Pi Durable, renew the verified guest session and test replay rejection. The answer comes from the published TYPO3 text below.

Open the live discovery document, OAuth server metadata and OpenAPI schema. Discovery is public. API calls require an administrator-registered personal agent, independent client and session assertions, and a fresh DPoP proof.

Example question: What does TYPO3 Lab say about Poppy?

Example answer: TYPO3 Lab implements Poppy draft 0.1 for verified guest sessions and published knowledge. Editors maintain the explanation in TYPO3. The API returns that text with its source URL.

This displayed answer is an editorial example. The authenticated API reads the section “What TYPO3 Lab says” above on every request.

• GET /.well-known/poppy.json — domain discovery.
  • GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/poppy — OAuth issuer metadata.
  • GET /poppy/openapi.json — supported operations and topics.
  • POST /poppy/token — verify assertions and start or renew a guest session.
  • GET /poppy/knowledge?topic=poppy — read the Poppy explanation with a fresh DPoP proof; pi-durable selects the second topic.
  • POST /poppy/revoke — revoke a session token.

The field guide lives under /agent-nexus/poppy/. The domain-level protocol URLs remain stable under /poppy. Moving the explanation does not change the issuer or require agents to register again.

• Domain-wide HTTPS discovery and reciprocal OAuth issuer metadata.
  • ES256 and RS256 agent authentication, short-lived assertions and atomic replay rejection.
  • Guest sessions, renewal, random opaque Session Tokens and DPoP key binding.
  • A read-only OpenAPI endpoint for explicitly selected, published English CMS text.
  • Ordinary signed-out website browsing.

Direct, device and mediated sign-in, Account Tokens, browser-session exchange, MCP and Poppy conversations are outside this release. They are not advertised by discovery. Existing TYPO3 MCP credentials do not become Poppy credentials.

See the official draft and Sierra’s announcement from 9 October 2026.

match.header: Where Poppy fits in Agent Nexus

set.header: Where Poppy fits in Agent Nexus
set.bodytext:
Agent Nexus is the lab’s shared field guide for six protocols. Each one solves a different part of an agent visit:

  • A2UI: describe an interface as data.
  • AG-UI: stream an agent’s work and request approval.
  • A2A: delegate a task to another agent.
  • UCP: discover a merchant and prepare a checkout.
  • AP2: prove a purchase was authorised.
  • Poppy: identify the personal agent and establish the person’s permitted access.

MCP exposes tools; OpenAPI describes HTTP operations. Poppy can give a personal agent a session for those channels. Our current profile advertises only its read-only OpenAPI channel. Agent Nexus supplies five protocol demos; the independent Poppy extension supplies this sixth experiment.

On 9 October 2026 Sierra published a first draft of the Personal Agent Protocol, nicknamed Poppy (Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor, Sierra). Three days earlier Sierra had announced the protocol together with Meta, Genesys, Instinct, NiCE, Rocket, Shopify, Stripe and Walmart (Sierra, 6 October 2026). With the draft, 35 more companies joined as design partners to shape it, among them Adyen, Bank of America, Cloudflare, Mastercard, OpenAI, PayPal, Target, Visa and Zapier.

The problem it addresses: a personal agent often has to log in as its person and click through pages built for humans. Businesses have no standard way to recognise such an agent, to see whom it represents or to guide what it does. Poppy splits the control: the person decides how much access the agent gets, and the business decides what an agent may do. A company can serve agents through its existing website and APIs or through an agent of its own.

match.header: The five building blocks — and what this lab implements

set.header: The five building blocks — and what this lab implements
set.bodytext:
1. Discovery: a company publishes a standard file at /.well-known/poppy.json. It tells agents how to work with the company, how people sign in and what an agent can do. In the lab: implemented — open our discovery document.
  2. Sessions: an agent starts a session for its person and identifies itself, so the company knows an agent is acting. A guest session already answers questions such as stock levels or a returns policy. In the lab: verified guest sessions with renewal.
  3. Sign-in: when a task needs the person’s account, the person signs in on the company’s own page with OAuth. If the company allows it, the agent then receives a token limited to the access the person approved. In the lab: not part of this release.
  4. One session across every channel: one token works on the website, the APIs and the company’s agent, and the steps before and after sign-in count as one visit. Nobody starts over, and the company sees the whole journey. In the lab: the session covers our single OpenAPI channel.
  5. Getting the job done: each company chooses its channels — ordinary web pages with permissions checked on every page, APIs described with OpenAPI or MCP, or its own agent for conversations such as a warranty claim, with streamed replies and requests that can wait for updates. In the lab: a read-only OpenAPI endpoint for published TYPO3 text.

Source: Sierra, “Sharing a draft of Personal Agent Protocol”. The draft specification defines each block in detail.

match.header: Built on standards companies already run

set.header: Built on standards companies already run
set.bodytext:
Poppy builds on OAuth, JSON Web Tokens, HTTPS, OpenAPI and MCP, so teams can use libraries they already know, start with the infrastructure they have and add channels later. A company connects once through Poppy instead of building a separate integration for every agent, and industries can extend the core with layers of their own (Sierra).

Sierra describes Poppy as complementary to shopping protocols such as the Universal Commerce Protocol. UCP covers finding products, checking out and managing orders; Poppy covers who the agent is, what its person allowed and any kind of task, from buying clothes to applying for a mortgage. Agent Nexus runs both side by side: compare Poppy with our UCP demo.

• Return a jacket through the website: the agent finds the retailer through Poppy and identifies itself, and its person signs in once. The agent uses the normal returns page and can start the return, but it cannot change the payment details on file.
  • Rebook a cancelled flight through APIs: with the access its person approved, the agent connects to the airline’s booking tools over MCP, finds the next available flight and confirms the seat with its person before booking.
  • Get a mortgage pre-approval through the company’s agent: at Sierra Summit, Alex McGillis, VP of Product at Rocket, showed Meta’s personal agent Muse finding Rocket’s agent through Poppy and asking for permission to connect. He signed in to share his credit and income details. The two agents worked through purchase price, down payment and interest rate, and a pre-approval letter was ready within moments, with Alex in control throughout (demo on X, Sierra Summit 2026 recap).

Source: Sierra, 9 October 2026. TYPO3 Lab does not implement these account scenarios yet. It shows the signed-out part: discovery, a verified guest session and a sourced answer.

Over the month after the draft, Sierra plans design workshops and a reference implementation for developers, and it invites more companies to read the draft and contribute (Sierra). The draft is published at personalagentprotocol.org.

TYPO3 Lab follows draft 0.1. When the draft or the reference implementation changes, the typo3-poppy extension and this page follow.

1. Bret Taylor, Clay Bavor: Sharing a draft of Personal Agent Protocol. Sierra, 9 October 2026.
  2. Bret Taylor, Clay Bavor: Introducing Personal Agent Protocol. Sierra, 6 October 2026.
  3. Personal Agent Protocol specification, draft. personalagentprotocol.org.
  4. Sierra: Sierra Summit 2026 recap.
  5. Sierra on X: the Rocket and Muse demo of Personal Agent Protocol.

The summaries above are TYPO3 Lab’s own wording of these sources.

set.description: Use Pi Durable on Cloudflare to discover TYPO3 through Poppy and read a published explanation with a source URL.

set.header: Keep the personal agent’s work durable
set.subheadline: A durable personal agent calls the TYPO3 Lab knowledge API through Poppy. Its session state survives between tool calls.

set.bodytext:
Pi Durable provides the runtime for a personal agent whose conversations and tool work need to survive interruptions. Poppy provides the interface to the company. TYPO3 provides the editable, published knowledge.

In our example, a Pi tool discovers TYPO3 Lab, verifies its issuer, starts a signed-out session and reads the Poppy explanation. The tool returns only the published answer and its source URL to the model. Signing keys, DPoP keys and Session Tokens stay in private durable storage.

The example includes a protocol client and a Cloudflare Agents SDK PiHarness integration. Its transport is tested against TYPO3 locally. Cloudflare deployment and live model inference require a configured caller origin and authenticated application routing.

set.content: Pi Durable keeps the agent’s work and private protocol state. Poppy connects that agent to the lab. TYPO3 returns the editor-maintained explanation. Resuming an agent run reuses the stored identity and renews the guest session when necessary.

set.header: Example: ask the lab, keep the source
set.bodytext:
You: What does TYPO3 Lab say about Poppy, and how does Pi Durable fit?

Pi tool: read_typo3_lab({"topic":"poppy"}), followed by read_typo3_lab({"topic":"pi-durable"}).

Expected assistant response: The lab offers verified guest sessions and a read-only API for its published explanations. Pi Durable runs the personal agent and preserves its work; Poppy carries the requests; TYPO3 owns the content. Sources: the Poppy and Pi Durable feature pages.

This is an example transcript, not a claim that a live model ran on this page. The included integration test runs the discovery, session, renewal and content requests against TYPO3.

Try this topic in the live protocol playground. The playground verifies Poppy requests in your browser. The Pi Durable source example adds a model and durable runtime.

set.bodytext:
Brendan Irvine-Broque’s Poppy demo post links a two-Worker example with a simulated order exchange. Our example uses the same personal-agent/company separation for published TYPO3 knowledge.

The source lives in Examples/pi-durable in the extension repository. It includes pinned dependencies, a Worker entry point, a WebCrypto protocol client, tests and setup instructions. set.title: Poppy help: install, connect and test
set.seo_title: Poppy help: install, connect and test | TYPO3 Lab
set.description: Install the TYPO3 Poppy extension, register a personal agent, edit published answers and diagnose protocol errors.

set.subheadline: Install the extension, connect a registered agent and keep the lab’s explanation current in TYPO3.

set.bodytext:
Require webconsulting/typo3-poppy from our GitLab repository, run TYPO3 extension setup and flush caches. Enable poppy.enabled on the domain’s canonical root site. The discovery file belongs at /.well-known/poppy.json, not under a language or site path.

Configure the organisation name, exact allowed client metadata URLs and topic sources in the site’s poppy configuration. A source selects one public page slug and one text-section heading. The extension README contains the full configuration.

1. Open Agent Nexus → Poppy in the TYPO3 Page module.
  2. Edit the normal text element headed “What TYPO3 Lab says”.
  3. Publish your change using the normal TYPO3 workflow.
  4. Call the knowledge API again. It reads the current published record.

The Pi Durable page has its own answer under the same heading. Hidden, scheduled, workspace-only, group-protected and x402-gated records are not returned. The first release serves English source records.

1. Install the locked dependencies in Examples/pi-durable.
  2. Set the public HTTPS TYPO3 origin, caller origin and Workers AI model.
  3. Deploy the Worker in your Cloudflare account and register its /agent.json URL in the TYPO3 site configuration.
  4. Connect LabAssistant.ask through your application’s authenticated, user-scoped routing.
  5. Ask the agent to read the Poppy and Pi Durable topics.

The example Worker publishes client metadata and public signing keys. Private keys and Session Tokens remain in durable storage. Its generic agent routes are not publicly exposed.

• invalid_client: check the exact allowlist URL, public metadata, same-host HTTPS JWKS, signing algorithm and assertion audience.
  • invalid_grant: create fresh independent assertions. Check expiry, clock and unique assertion IDs.
  • invalid_dpop_proof: sign the current HTTP method and URL without query or fragment. Use the bound key and the token hash. Never reuse a proof.
  • invalid_session: start a new guest session. Do not reuse another agent’s or user’s session ID.
  • not_found: check the configured topic, source slug, exact section heading and publication permissions.
  • rate_limited: wait for the response’s Retry-After interval.

Guest sessions grant no account scopes. Requests for account scopes are rejected. Tokens belong in the Authorization header.

Test Poppy in your browser: choose a topic, ask the lab, renew the session and test replay protection. Expand “See the requests” to inspect HTTP outcomes. The playground uses the same published CMS content as external personal agents.

The extension’s Build/Scripts/runTests.sh runs the PHP unit suite and syntax checks. The Pi Durable example has transport tests, TypeScript checks and a Worker dry build. The lab’s Build/Scripts/test-poppy.sh runs authenticated requests against DDEV, verifies renewal and replay rejection, then removes its temporary test identity.

set.bodytext: Explore Poppy in Agent Nexus, the lab’s home for agent protocols. Poppy adds identity and limited access for personal agents. Read the explanation, try a verified guest session or follow the Pi Durable example.
Install Poppy, register an agent and troubleshoot requests. Follow the Pi Durable example to connect a durable personal agent to the lab.

The lab includes the standalone webconsulting/typo3-poppy extension: domain discovery, verified guest sessions, DPoP proofs and a read-only OpenAPI content endpoint. See the supported draft 0.1 profile.

set.header: Six agent protocols running on TYPO3
set.bodytext:
Explore how a personal agent identifies itself, builds interfaces, streams its work, delegates tasks and prepares purchases. Agent Nexus brings six protocols together in one field guide: A2UI, AG-UI, A2A, UCP, AP2 and Poppy.

Choose a protocol below, read how it works and try its demo. The first five run sandbox workflows; Poppy makes verified, read-only requests to published TYPO3 knowledge. Nothing is charged or sent to another person.

Identity and access → Poppy. Start here to understand how a site recognises a personal agent. Continue to A2UI for interfaces, AG-UI for streaming and approvals, A2A for delegated tasks, UCP for checkout and AP2 for payment authorisation.

Use the shared playground to compare the five embedded demos, or open the Poppy playground to discover the lab, start a session and request a sourced explanation. The Pi Durable example shows how the calling agent can preserve its work.

Try A2UI, AG-UI, A2A, UCP and AP2 in the five embedded demos below. Each uses its own endpoint. For identity and access, open the Poppy playground: discover the lab, start a verified guest session, read published knowledge, renew the session and test replay rejection.

match.header: Poppy — identify the agent and read published knowledge

set.header: Poppy — identify the agent and read published knowledge
set.bodytext: Open the Poppy playground. Select Poppy or Pi Durable, choose “Ask the lab”, renew the session and test replay protection. Inspect “See the requests” to follow the protocol. Read how it works · Help and troubleshooting.

Agent Nexus is a field guide to six protocols. Its bundled extension implements A2UI, AG-UI, A2A, UCP and AP2; the independent TYPO3 Poppy extension adds personal-agent identity and guest access. Each protocol has an explanation and a working demo.
